chunks: And it was narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Nahdī, who said:

Saʿīd al-Aʿraj asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, while I was with him, about a khamīṣah whose warp was silk and whose weft was goat wool. So he said: "There is no harm in entering ihram in it; rather, what is disliked is that which is made purely of it."

key_terms.الْخَالِصُ: that which is pure or unmixed
key_terms.الْخَمِيصَةِ: a garment or cloth being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.تُحْرِمَ: to enter the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to enter ihram wearing a garment mixed with silk?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning clothing worn in the state of ihram. It indicates that a garment mixed from silk and goat wool is permissible for ihram, while dislike applies to what is made purely of silk.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2611 - It was narrated from Abu al-Hasan al-Nahdi, who said:

Sa'id al-A'raj asked Abu Abdullah (as) in my presence about a garment (khamiṣah) whose warp was made of silk (ibrīsīm) and its weft was made of goat wool (mir‘izzā).
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in entering Ihram in it. What is disliked is the garment made entirely of silk."
